title: Self-Consistency Improves the Trustworthiness of Self-Interpretable GNNs
claim: Self-inconsistency between repeated explanations concentrates on unimportant features, while important features stay nearly perfectly consistent across models and datasets.
layout: 8 small box-plot panels in one row, shared y-axis, UNIMP vs IMP
description: A single horizontal strip of eight narrow box-plot panels sharing one y-axis labeled DIFF, scaled up to 4.5×10^-1. Panels pair two self-interpretable GNNs, SMGNN and GSAT, with four datasets labeled A to D. Each panel has two boxes, UNIMP and IMP. The UNIMP boxes are orange and tall, with medians above zero and long whiskers. The IMP boxes are flattened to near-zero black lines. The contrast repeats in every panel, so the eye goes first to the tall orange boxes and then to the flat IMP lines beside them. Panel C (Benzene) shows small values for both features. The design is spare, with no legend and only two colors.
caption: Self-inconsistency measured as the L1 difference (DIFF) between two explanations. Results are shown for SMGNN (Azzolin et al., 2025b) and GSAT (Miao et al., 2022) across four benchmark datasets: A = BA-2MOTIFS, B = MR, C = BENZENE, D = MUTAGENICITY. Within each panel, UNIMP and IMP denote unimportant and important features, respectively.
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) achieve strong predictive performance but offer limited transparency in their decision-making. Self-Interpretable GNNs (SI-GNNs) address this by generating built-in explanations, yet their training objectives are misaligned with evaluation criteria such as faithfulness. This raises two key questions: (i) can faithfulness be explicitly optimized during training, and (ii) does such optimization truly improve explanation quality? We show that faithfulness is intrinsically tied to explanation self-consistency and can therefore be optimized directly. Empirical analysis further reveals that self-inconsistency predominantly occurs on unimportant features, linking it to redundancy-driven explanation inconsistency observed in recent work and suggesting untapped potential for improving explanation quality. Building on these insights, we introduce a simple, model-agnostic self-consistency (SC) fine-tuning strategy. Without changing model architectures, SC consistently improves explanation quality across multiple dimensions and benchmarks, offering an effective and scalable pathway to more trustworthy GNN explanations. Our code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/ICDM-UESTC/SelfConsistencyXGNN}.
